examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Press “What is your return policy?”. Its answer opens and the shipping answer closes. Press the same heading again to close it.

examples.title: Multiple
examples.caption: Open Privacy and security. Notification settings stays open; close either section independently.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.caption: Tab to Premium feature information. It stays focusable, and pressing it leaves its panel closed. Try “How do I update my email address?” instead.

examples.title: Collapsible
examples.caption: Open Timeline, then press it again. It stays open until you choose another heading.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Press Security to open it, then press it again. Cancel the confirmation and Security stays open; accept it and the section closes.

examples.title: Keep Mounted
examples.caption: Write a message, switch to Formatting, then return to Reply to this thread. Your draft is still there.

examples.title: Find in Page
examples.caption: Use your browser’s Find command to search for “pineapple”. The closed “Which fruit do you stock?” panel opens to reveal the match.

examples.title: Deep Link
examples.caption: Press Jump to the refund timeline. The closed Refunds panel opens and the browser moves to the linked paragraph.

examples.title: Animation
examples.caption: Open or close an item. Its panel animates its height.

examples.title: Expand All
examples.caption: Press Expand all or Collapse all. Open an individual week near the bottom to scroll it into view after its panel opens.

examples.title: Nested
examples.caption: Open Billing, then Invoices inside it. The inner accordion changes without closing Billing.

examples.title: FAQ Search
examples.caption: Search for “refund” to show and open matching answers. Try “zzz” for the empty result, then clear the search to restore all questions.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: Each step is an h4 with its number and a Show or Hide hint that follows its open state. Open Import the parts to see it update.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Open the dialog with Enter to start on Cancel. Tab stays inside, clicking outside leaves it open, and Escape closes it and returns focus to the trigger.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Choose Review Changes, then Keep Editing or Discard.

examples.title: Shortcut
examples.caption: Press Cmd+Shift+H (Ctrl+Shift+H on Windows and Linux) to open the dialog without clicking.

examples.title: Animation
examples.caption: Open and close the dialog. It slides up and fades in, and slides down and fades out before it unmounts.

examples.title: Nested
examples.caption: Choose Delete Workspace, then Delete. Press Escape to step back to the first question, or choose Delete Workspace to close both.

examples.title: Async Action
examples.caption: Choose Delete Project, then Delete. The first attempt fails so you can try again. While Deleting… is shown, Cancel and Escape leave the dialog open. A successful retry closes it.

examples.title: Confirm From Anywhere
examples.caption: Choose Archive Project, then Archive or Cancel. The console shows the answer.

examples.title: Confirm
examples.caption: Delete a project. Cancel or Escape keeps it; Delete removes it and focuses a neighboring row's button. Reset Projects brings the list back.

examples.title: Queued Questions
examples.caption: Choose Review Two Projects. Answer the Acme question, then the Globex question. The console shows both answers once the second one is in.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Select the inset portrait to view the profile. The initials fill the same recess while the image loads.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Click Button, or focus it and press Enter or Space. The console logs each press.

examples.title: Pending
examples.caption: Press Save, then press it again while it saves. Nothing happens until the first action finishes.

examples.title: Pending Content
examples.caption: Press Save. Its arrow turns into a spinner while it saves.

examples.title: Handling Errors
examples.caption: Choose Save Changes. Saving always fails here: the console shows the error and the label changes to Try Again.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.caption: Try clicking the button. It does nothing, and Tab skips it.

examples.title: Focusable When Disabled
examples.caption: Focus Title, then press Tab to reach Publish while it is disabled. Enter a title to enable it, then choose Publish. The console logs what was published.

examples.title: Links
examples.caption: Choose Get Started to jump to Installation on this page. Changelog is disabled and does not navigate.

examples.title: Forms
examples.caption: Edit the email and choose Subscribe, or press Enter in the field. The console logs each submission, and Reset restores the original email.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Choose a date, then use Previous or Next to change the month. Arrow keys move through the days.

examples.title: Range
examples.caption: Choose a start date, then move to an end date to preview the range. Choose the end to finish, or press Escape to cancel the unfinished range.

examples.title: Multiple
examples.caption: Choose another date to add it, or choose a selected date to remove it.

examples.title: Unavailable Dates
examples.caption: Try an unavailable date, then choose an available one. Unavailable days remain focusable so their state can be heard.

examples.title: Min and Max
examples.caption: Move toward either end of the allowed dates. Keyboard navigation and month buttons stop at the limits.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.caption: Try choosing a date or changing months. A disabled calendar has no available controls.

examples.title: Read Only
examples.caption: Move through dates and months. The selected value stays unchanged.

examples.title: Two Months
examples.caption: Move between October and November with arrow keys. Next advances both visible months to December and January.

examples.title: Fixed Weeks
examples.caption: Move from February to March. Both grids keep six week rows, and dates outside each month are hidden.

examples.title: Month and Year Selects
examples.caption: Choose a year and month to jump directly to a birthday, then choose the day.

examples.title: Custom Month and Year Selects
examples.caption: Choose a month or a year from the selects. The calendar follows, and the arrow keys still move between days.

examples.title: Language
examples.caption: Move through the calendar. Month names, weekday headers, and full date labels are in German, with Monday first.

examples.title: Name Formats
examples.caption: The weekday headers are narrow and the heading uses short month names: Oct – Nov 2026.

examples.title: Custom Days
examples.caption: Choose a date to see its price selected with it. Dates outside the current month have no price.

examples.title: Range Limits
examples.caption: In October 2026, choose October 15 then October 20. This example accepts 3–8 days and allows the range to span the unavailable weekend.

examples.title: Range in Progress
examples.caption: Choose a start date, then move with the arrow keys. The console logs the start and each focused date until Enter picks the end.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Choose a date or change the month. The console logs each change and its reason.

examples.title: Today
examples.caption: Find the marked date for today in Pacific/Kiritimati, which may differ from today in your time zone.

examples.title: Driving It from Anywhere
examples.caption: Press Go to Christmas to select December 25 and move focus there, or Today to jump back to today and select it.

examples.title: Presets
examples.caption: Choose Last 7 Days, This Month or Next 30 Days. The range is selected and the calendar shows its start.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: The table is your own markup, built from the grid's state. Navigate and select as usual.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Click the checkbox or its label, or focus it and press Space, to accept the terms.

examples.title: Description
examples.caption: Click Accept terms and conditions. The field connects the label and description to the checkbox.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.caption: Security alerts are always on, so that checkbox is disabled. Clicking its label leaves it checked.

examples.title: Read-Only
examples.caption: Tab to the checked checkbox. Space and clicks leave the setting unchanged.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Change the checkbox, or press Toggle. The console logs each change and its reason.

examples.title: Forms
examples.caption: Create the account with the terms unchecked to see native validation, then accept them and try again. The console logs what was submitted, and Reset restores the defaults.

examples.title: Group
examples.caption: Choose several toppings. The group keeps one list of checked values.

examples.title: Parent Checkbox
examples.caption: Select all checks every topping. Uncheck one topping to put Select all into its mixed state.

examples.title: Disabled Group
examples.caption: The Backups group is disabled. In Sync folders, Select all changes the enabled folders while Desktop stays checked.

examples.title: Controlled Group
examples.caption: Choose working days, or press Select Weekdays or Clear. The console logs the group's value and the reason it changed.

examples.title: Group in a Form
examples.caption: Save with nothing checked to see the inline error. Choose a notification method and save; the console logs the submitted values.

examples.title: Table
examples.caption: Select rows individually, or use Select all in the header. The console logs how many are selected.

examples.title: Animation
examples.caption: Check and uncheck a task. The check scales and fades in, and out before it unmounts.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: Choose topics. Each checkbox renders a button that shows a check or a plus from its state.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Open Share, then close it with either Close button, Escape, or a press outside. Focus returns to Share.

examples.title: Scrollable Content
examples.caption: Open Scrollable Content in a short window. Scroll the terms while the title and Decline/Accept buttons stay in view.

examples.title: Forms
examples.caption: Open New Article and choose Save Draft or Publish. The console logs the submitted button's value. An empty title prevents submission.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Check Open or press Notification Settings, then close the dialog. The console logs each change, its reason and when it finishes.

examples.title: Keyboard Shortcut
examples.caption: Press Command+J or Control+J to open New contact. The button shows the keys, and Escape returns focus to it.

examples.title: Animation
examples.caption: Open the dialog and close it. The console logs when each animation finishes; focus returns as closing starts.

examples.title: Modal
examples.caption: Choose a mode, open Notes, and try Tab or clicking the page. Check Close on outside press to compare dismissal.

examples.title: Inside a Frame
examples.caption: Open Delete Draft. The dialog and its dim cover only the frame, and Tab stays inside the dialog.

examples.title: Warn Before Closing a Dirty Form
examples.caption: Type a post, then press Escape or click outside. Keep editing returns to the field; Discard closes the dialog and clears the draft.

examples.title: Nested Dialogs
examples.caption: Open Account, then Change Password. Press Escape once to return to Account, and again to close it.

examples.title: Opening from a Menu Item
examples.caption: Open File Actions and choose Rename. Close the dialog to return focus to the File Actions button.

examples.title: Opening from Anywhere
examples.caption: Open a reminder from either unpaid invoice, or press Open from Code. The same dialog shows that invoice, and the console logs how it closed.

examples.title: Presentation
examples.caption: Open Edit Profile as a sheet. On a touch screen, drag it down to dismiss it, or use Cancel or Save Changes.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: Open View Details. The trigger's label and the description come from their state, and Close renders as a link.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Press Username to focus the input, then type a name.

examples.title: Validation
examples.caption: Press Subscribe with an empty or invalid email, then correct it to clear the error.

examples.title: Field Sets
examples.caption: Move through the address fields. Their legend and description name the group.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Edit the website, then press Clear website. The text clears, focus returns to the input and the console logs the reason. Pressing https:// focuses the input too.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Press Shipping speed. Focus moves to the checked option, and a screen reader names the group Shipping speed.

examples.title: Slider
examples.caption: Press Volume, then use the arrow keys. The thumb moves, and a screen reader reads it as Volume.

examples.title: Switch
examples.caption: Press Email me product updates. The switch turns on.

examples.title: Wrapping a Control
examples.caption: Press Accept terms and conditions. The checkbox checks, and a double click doesn't select the text.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Press Open Menu and choose an item, with the pointer or the arrow keys and Enter. The menu closes and the console logs your choice.

examples.title: Submenus
examples.caption: Open Edit, then Find or Transform. Use the arrows to enter and leave each level; choosing an action closes the menu tree.

examples.title: Shortcuts
examples.caption: Open File to see shortcut hints for your platform. Choose an item to report its action; this markup example does not register global shortcuts.

examples.title: Icons
examples.caption: Open Share and type an item’s name. The icons aren’t part of the item’s accessible name or the text typeahead matches.

examples.title: Checkboxes
examples.caption: Open View and toggle Status bar or Minimap. The menu stays open so you can change several settings, and the console logs each one.

examples.title: Radio Group
examples.caption: Open Panel and choose a position. Only one item in each group is checked, the menu stays open, and the console logs the change.

examples.title: Context Menu
examples.caption: Right-click or long-press the area, or focus it and press Shift+F10. Choose an action and the console logs it.

examples.title: Disabled Items
examples.caption: Open Document and move through its items with the arrow keys. Disabled actions remain discoverable but cannot run; Locked cannot open a menu.

examples.title: Animation
examples.caption: Open Animated, then its More tools submenu, and close them. The console logs Opening or Closing, then when the animation finishes.

examples.title: Presentation
examples.caption: Open Options as a sheet, enter Move to, then go back or choose a destination. You can drag downward to dismiss the sheet.

examples.title: Triggers Outside the Menu
examples.caption: Open the actions for different files. One menu shows the active row; opening from code uses the same payload and reports the closing reason.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Open each section, then use Tab or the arrow keys to move through its links.

examples.title: Link Component
examples.caption: Choose a link to update the current page without reloading the example.

examples.title: Vertical
examples.caption: Use Up and Down between the sidebar items, then open a panel beside its trigger.

examples.title: Click Only
examples.caption: Click a trigger to open it. Moving the pointer between triggers does not open another panel.

examples.title: Nested
examples.caption: Open Components, then open Overlays or Forms. Escape closes the inner panel first.

examples.title: Animation
examples.caption: Switch between Guides and Components to see the viewport resize and the panels slide.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: Open Guides to see its render state, then compare the current link and disabled trigger.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Press Share to open the popover, then close it with Cancel, Copy Link, Escape, or a press outside. Focus returns to Share.

examples.title: Forms
examples.caption: Open Edit Profile, change the name, and press Save. The popover closes and the console logs the saved name.

examples.title: Keep It Open While Editing
examples.caption: Open Add Note, type something, then press Escape or click outside. Keep Editing returns to the field; Discard closes the popover and clears the note.

examples.title: Placement
examples.caption: Choose a side and an alignment, then open Delivery. Near a window edge, the popover flips or shifts to stay visible.

examples.title: Offsets
examples.caption: Change the offsets and the padding, then open Delivery. The popover moves away from the trigger and along it.

examples.title: Arrow
examples.caption: Open Help, then press Top, Right, Bottom, or Left. The popover stays open while it and its arrow move to that side.

examples.title: Anchor
examples.caption: Press the filters button. The popover lines up with the search field instead of the small button beside it.

examples.title: Modal
examples.caption: Choose a mode, open Add Comment, and try Tab or clicking the page.

examples.title: Focus
examples.caption: Open each one: Rename focuses its field, Publish focuses its Publish button, and Status leaves focus on the trigger.

examples.title: Open on Hover
examples.caption: Hover @kofi, then move into the popover and press Follow. You can also open it by pressing the trigger.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Check Open or press Set Status, then close the popover. The console logs each change and its reason.

examples.title: Keyboard Shortcut
examples.caption: Press Command+I or Control+I to open Invite. Press the same shortcut again, or Escape, to close it.

examples.title: Triggers Outside the Popover
examples.caption: Edit Inès Moreau or Kofi Mensah and save a new role. The owner can't be edited. Edit Newest Member opens the same editor from code, and the console logs how it closed.

examples.title: Animation
examples.caption: Open What's New, then press Got It. The console logs Opening, Open, Closing, and Closed.

examples.title: Presentation
examples.caption: Open Add Reminder as a sheet. Dismiss it with Cancel, Save, Escape, the dimmed area, or a downward swipe on a touch screen.

examples.title: In Place
examples.caption: Open Feedback. The panel opens above the button, inside the corner box.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: Open Show Updates. The trigger's label comes from its state, the title renders as an h3, and Close renders as a link.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Read the export bar. Its label and 60% value are available both visually and to a screen reader.

examples.title: Indeterminate
examples.caption: Read the Connecting to server bar. It shows an ongoing task without announcing a percentage.

examples.title: Changing the Value
examples.caption: Click Upload Next to add one photo, or 20%, and watch the console count them. At 100%, the button stops advancing the bar. Click Reset to start at 0%.

examples.title: Bounds
examples.caption: Compare step 3 of 5 with the fill. Because the range starts at 1, the value is halfway through the range.

examples.title: Format and Locale
examples.caption: Compare the progress readings. They show downloaded data, a precise percentage, time remaining, and a localized percentage.

examples.title: Value Label
examples.caption: Read Copying files with a screen reader. It announces 3 of 12 files and 25%, while the visible value stays compact.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Choose Express, then use the arrow keys to move the selection between speeds.

examples.title: Description
examples.caption: Choose Weekly digest by its label. Each radio is also described by the line under it.

examples.title: Choice Card
examples.caption: Click anywhere on the Pro card to choose it. Arrow keys move the selection between cards too.

examples.title: Fieldset and Legend
examples.caption: Choose Yearly. The legend and the line under it describe both billing periods.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.caption: The Theme group is disabled. In Backups, Hourly is disabled, so the arrow keys move between Daily and Weekly.

examples.title: Read-Only
examples.caption: Click Team, or focus Pro and press the Down arrow. Pro stays checked.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Choose Starter, then press Choose Team. The console logs each change and its reason.

examples.title: Form
examples.caption: Choose Express and press Continue. The console logs the submitted value, and Reset returns the choice to Standard.

examples.title: Validation
examples.caption: Press Save without a choice to see the error. Choose SMS only and save again; the console logs the saved value.

examples.title: Animation
examples.caption: Hover Light to preview its dot, then choose it. The dot scales in on Light and out of System.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: Choose Nothing. Each radio renders a full-width button that shows a check from its state.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Open Role and choose Editor. The list closes and the trigger shows your choice.

examples.title: Items as Data
examples.caption: Open Plan to see the options, separator, and Contact sales group. Education is disabled; choose Enterprise to update the value.

examples.title: Groups
examples.caption: Open Font and choose from Sans serif, Serif or Monospace. Each group has a label that screen readers announce.

examples.title: Icons
examples.caption: Choose Center or End. Both the label and the icon in the trigger update to match the selected item.

examples.title: Typeahead
examples.caption: Focus Country and type “sw” to select Sweden without opening the list. Open it and type “g” to highlight Germany, then press Enter.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.caption: Billing country is disabled and Shipping from is read-only. Open Shipping to and press the arrow keys: the highlight skips Denmark, which can't be chosen.

examples.title: Clear Button
examples.caption: Press the clear button. The trigger shows Unassigned, focus returns to it, and the console logs null. Choose someone to bring the button back.

examples.title: Multiple
examples.caption: Choose several languages, then choose one again to remove it. The list stays open, and the console logs the array.

examples.title: Select All
examples.caption: Open Regions and press Select all. Press it again to clear the selection, then choose one region to see the mixed state.

examples.title: Search with Groups
examples.caption: Open Country and type “ja”. Only Asia Pacific and Japan remain. Try “zz” to see the empty message, then clear the search to show every country.

examples.title: Async Search
examples.caption: Open Country and type “an”. Results arrive after a short delay. Clear the search and move or scroll to the last result to load another page.

examples.title: Object Values
examples.caption: Inès starts selected even though the initial value is a copy of her item. Choose another assignee; the console logs the ID the form submits.

examples.title: Virtualized
examples.caption: Open Item and press End to reach Item 10000, then Home to return to the beginning. Scroll through the list; only nearby rows render.

examples.title: Align Item with Trigger
examples.caption: Open Priority: Medium sits over the trigger. Close it, uncheck Align item with trigger, and open it again to compare placement.

examples.title: Scrollable
examples.caption: Open Time zone and move down with the arrow keys. The list scrolls to keep the highlighted option visible.

examples.title: Invalid
examples.caption: Press Continue without choosing a shipping method to show the error. Choose one and continue; the console logs the submitted value.

examples.title: Forms
examples.caption: Choose a country and some topics, change Frequency, then press Save; the console logs all three fields. Reset restores the initial choices.

examples.title: Presentation
examples.caption: Open Status to show the bottom sheet. Choose an option to close it, or drag down to dismiss it without changing the value.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Drag the thumb, or focus it and use the arrow keys, to adjust Volume.

examples.title: Range
examples.caption: Move either end of Price. The thumbs stay in order.

examples.title: Multiple Thumbs
examples.caption: Adjust Low, Medium and High independently, without moving one past another.

examples.title: Vertical
examples.caption: Drag up or down, or use the arrow keys, to adjust Bass and Treble.

examples.title: Field
examples.caption: Click the Volume label to focus the thumb, then use the arrow keys to change the value.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.caption: Brightness keeps its value, but can't be focused or dragged.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Drag either Temperature thumb to log the range and its reason. Reset sets the value from outside.

examples.title: Step and Bounds
examples.caption: Move Year in steps of five, and Opacity in steps of 0.05.

examples.title: Large Step
examples.caption: Focus Zoom and press an arrow key to move 1%, then Page Up, Page Down or Shift with an arrow key to move 25%.

examples.title: Distance Between Thumbs
examples.caption: Move either end of Opening hours. The thumbs stay at least four hours apart.

examples.title: Format and Locale
examples.caption: Adjust Budget, Opacity, Weight, Duration and Preis to compare currency, a percentage, a unit, a custom function and German formatting.

examples.title: Saving on Commit
examples.caption: Drag Brightness and release it, or press an arrow key. The console logs the value once, when you let go.

examples.title: Controller
examples.caption: Use Mute, Louder and Focus to operate Volume from outside the slider. The console logs each change with the imperative reason, and Read logs the value.

examples.title: Form
examples.caption: Adjust the filters and press Save to log the submitted values. Distance sits outside the form and joins it by id. Reset restores the defaults.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: Focus or drag the Brightness thumb to show its value above it.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Click Airplane mode, or focus the switch and press Space, to turn it on and off.

examples.title: Description
examples.caption: Click Weekly digest. The field connects the label and description to the switch.

examples.title: Choice Card
examples.caption: Click anywhere on the Public profile card to turn it on. Each card's switch keeps its own value.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.caption: Security alerts are always on, so that switch is disabled. Clicking it leaves it on, and Tab skips it.

examples.title: Read-Only
examples.caption: Tab to Encrypt backups. Space and clicks leave it on.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Turn Wi-Fi off, or press Toggle. The console logs each change and its reason.

examples.title: Form
examples.caption: Turn on Product updates and press Save. The console logs the submitted values, and Reset restores the defaults.

examples.title: Validation
examples.caption: Press Continue with the switch off to see the error. Turn on Two-factor authentication and continue; the console logs the submitted value.

examples.title: Saving on Toggle
examples.caption: Turn on Automatic backups. The thumb shows a spinner while it saves, then the switch turns on.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: Turn on Dark mode. The thumb renders a sun or a moon from its state.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Choose Password to show its panel. Use the left and right arrow keys to move between the tabs.

examples.title: Vertical
examples.caption: Focus General, then press Down Arrow to choose Security. Up Arrow moves back through the vertical list.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.caption: Use the arrow keys to reach Reports. It can receive focus, but pressing it leaves the current panel selected.

examples.title: Icons
examples.caption: Choose Replies. Its directional icon mirrors when the surrounding page uses right-to-left text.

examples.title: Manual Activation
examples.caption: Focus Preview, then press Right Arrow. Code receives focus; press Enter or Space to show its panel. Tab then moves into the Source field.

examples.title: Loop
examples.caption: Focus Year and press Right Arrow. Focus stays at the end because looping is off.

examples.title: Indicator
examples.caption: Choose Podcasts, then choose Vertical. The same indicator measures and follows the selected tab in either layout.

examples.title: Keep Mounted
examples.caption: Write a message, switch to Formatting, then return to Reply. Your draft is still there.

examples.title: Find in Page
examples.caption: Use your browser’s Find command to search for “restocking fee”. Returns opens to reveal the match.

examples.title: Animation
examples.caption: Move between Overview, Activity and Settings. The panels slide in the direction you moved.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Choose Drafts, then press Show Sent Mail. The console logs each new value with its reason.

examples.title: Links
examples.caption: Choose Activity. Its panel opens and the URL hash changes. Modified clicks keep the link’s usual browser behavior.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: Each tab renders its own button with an unread count after the label. Choose Unread to see who wrote to you.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Click Message to focus the textarea, then type. Press Enter to start a new line.

examples.title: Field
examples.caption: Click Feedback to focus the textarea. A screen reader reads the description with the field.

examples.title: Auto Resize
examples.caption: Type several lines in Notes. The textarea grows with each line until it reaches its maximum height, then scrolls. Delete the lines and it shrinks back.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Edit Bio and watch the character count under it. The textarea stops accepting text at 160 characters.

examples.title: Form
examples.caption: Type a message and press Send Message. The console logs it and the textarea clears. Pressing Send Message while it's empty is blocked.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.caption: Try to edit Reply or reach it with Tab. The disabled textarea keeps its value but can't be changed.

examples.title: Invalid
examples.caption: Focus Review. The textarea is marked invalid, and the error below says how long the review should be.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Press Create Event. Choose Undo, swipe the toast away, or wait for it to close. Undo logs Event removed.

examples.title: Types
examples.caption: Choose a type. Each toast shows its type's icon, and Loading turns into Photos uploaded when it finishes.

examples.title: Position
examples.caption: Choose a side and an alignment, then press Create Event and look for the toast at that edge of the page.

examples.title: Action and Cancel
examples.caption: Press Archive Message, then choose Undo or Dismiss, swipe the toast away, or let it time out. The console logs why it closed.

examples.title: Link
examples.caption: Press Send Invoice, then follow View in the toast.

examples.title: Promise
examples.caption: Press Save Changes to see Saving changes become Changes saved. Press it again for the error, then choose Retry.

examples.title: Stacking
examples.caption: Press Add Toast a few times, then hover the stack to expand it. Past four toasts, the rest wait their turn. Check Always expanded to keep it open.

examples.title: Duration
examples.caption: Press each button. Hover a toast to pause its timer. The session toast stays until you press Got It.

examples.title: Update and Dismiss
examples.caption: Press Upload Report and watch one toast count up to Report uploaded. Cancel Upload closes it early, and Dismiss All clears every toast.

examples.title: Async Action
examples.caption: Press Delete File, then Undo. The button shows Restoring… until the restore finishes, then the toast closes.

examples.title: Keyboard Shortcut
examples.caption: Press Send Message, then Alt+T (Option+T on a Mac) to focus the toast. Press Escape to dismiss it, or Alt+T again to go back.

examples.title: Overlay Host and Confirm
examples.caption: Press Delete on a project and confirm. The row goes away and a toast says so. Reset Projects brings them back.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: Press New Message to show a toast with Hollis Grant's initials. Choose Reply or close it.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: Press the star beside Q3 Roadmap, or focus it and press Enter or Space. It fills in while pressed, and its accessible name stays Star.

examples.title: Group
examples.caption: Press Bold and Italic to keep both pressed. Left and Right move focus without changing either.

examples.title: Single Selection
examples.caption: Press Align center to replace Align start, then press Align center again. One alignment always stays pressed.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: Press Favorite. The heart renders filled or empty from the toggle's pressed state.

examples.title: Overview
examples.caption: The tooltip starts open. Hover the button or reach it with Tab to show it again, and Escape closes it while focus stays on the button.

examples.title: Side
examples.caption: Hover Top, Left, Right and Bottom. Each tooltip opens on that side of its button, or flips into the middle when there isn't room.

examples.title: Anchor
examples.caption: Hover the help button. The tooltip opens below the Webhook URL field and lines up with its start, not with the button.

examples.title: Keyboard Shortcut
examples.caption: Hover Save or Share to read its shortcut, then press the button or the keys. The console logs Saved or Shared.

examples.title: Disabled Buttons
examples.caption: Hover or focus Publish to learn what's missing. Type a title, and Publish works and its tooltip goes away.

examples.title: Touch
examples.caption: Press the info button to open the tip, including on a touch screen. Press it again or anywhere else to close it.

examples.title: Keep Open on Press
examples.caption: Hover the copy button and press it. The tooltip stays open and changes to Copied.

examples.title: Truncated Text
examples.caption: Hover or focus each file. Only names that are cut off open a tooltip.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.caption: Check Open, or hover Export. The console logs each change and its reason.

examples.title: Shared
examples.caption: Move along Bold, Italic and Underline. One tooltip follows the pointer and shows each button's label.

examples.title: Animation
examples.caption: Hover Archive, then move away. The tooltip grows out of the button and fades, and the console logs Opening, Open, Closing and Closed.

examples.title: Custom Rendering
examples.caption: Hover Changelog. The trigger renders as a link, and its tooltip says where it goes.
